newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: AT&T says premature to talk of STET stake.
newsitem.headline: AT&T says premature to talk of STET stake.

text.p: John Walter, president and chief operating officer of AT&T Corp, said on Wednesday it was too early to talk about taking an equity stake in STET after news AT&T had forged an alliance with the Italian telecoms group.

Asked in a telephone interview with Reuters whether AT&T would cement the deal with an equity stake he said: "I think it's premature at this particular point to speculate on that. The Italian government has yet to define specifics associated with the (planned) privatisation."

The Italian government said earlier on Wednesday AT&T could become a shareholder in STET once it has been privatised in the Autumn. STET's statutes envisage a maximum three percent stake for private shareholders with the possibility of five percent with Treasury approval.

Asked if AT&T wanted a stake in STET Walter said the most important thing was that AT&T had a very strong alliance that satisfied its customers' expectations. "That does not require an equity investment but at the same time equity investments... do create a stronger business model and it's something we're open to," Walter said in the telephone interview.
Walter was speaking in a telephone interview from Rome ahead of a joint news conference with partners from STET/Telecom Italia and Unisource to amplify on Wednesday's alliance news.
In Europe STET/Telecom Italia is joining the AT&T-Unisource pan-European business telecoms joint venture.
AT&T-Unisource is currently 60 percent held by Unisource, the Netherlands-based joint venture between Dutch PTT, Telia of Sweden and Swiss Telecom PTT. AT&T holds the rest.
In Latin America, STET/Telecom Italia and AT&T will form a 50-50 joint venture that will deliver a portfolio of global services.
Walter said AT&T would be looking closely at STET working towards a definitive alliance agreement by year end.

"As we go through that we will look at all options as they relate to making sure we create the strongest business platform to serve the needs of our customers," he said. -- Keiron Henderson, Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
